annotations.keyFindings: At a month-3 score of 30 or below, sensitivity was 0.71 and specificity 0.68 for separation within 12 months among 412 residents; the area under the ROC curve was 0.74 and the positive predictive value 0.35.
annotations.limitations: Two hospitals; the threshold was examined in the same data that produced the estimate; separation prevalence of 19 percent may differ locally.

annotations.keyFindings: The 15-item self-rating was internally consistent (alpha 0.88) and stable over two weeks (0.81); scores were lowest at months 3 to 4.
annotations.limitations: No comparison with later separation; measures experienced difficulty, not intention to leave.

annotations.keyFindings: Across 24 studies, 12-month retention was 78 to 94 percent with a residency and 64 to 88 percent without; no study evaluated a screening step.
annotations.limitations: Mostly single-organisation before-after studies; inconsistent retention definitions; search ended in 2020.

annotations.keyFindings: Stated intention to leave at month 6 identified 30 of 62 later leavers (sensitivity 0.48) with specificity 0.86.
annotations.limitations: Single question; early-career rather than residency nurses; one health system.

annotations.keyFindings: Separation dates in human resources records were present and correct for 99 percent of leavers; reason codes misclassified internal transfers as resignations in 23 percent.
annotations.limitations: Three hospitals; manager confirmation used as the check.

annotations.keyFindings: Twelve-month retention rose from 81 to 88 percent after a booster for residents in the lowest quarter of the self-rating; uptake was 64 percent.
annotations.limitations: Uncontrolled before-after comparison with a new allowance and a hiring freeze in the same period.

annotations.keyFindings: Across 11 hospitals, the positive predictive value of a fixed threshold ranged from 0.21 to 0.44 as separation varied from 12 to 27 percent; later seminars lowered sensitivity.
annotations.limitations: Hospital-level comparison; threshold timing varied between sites.

claims.text: At a month-3 score of 30 or below, a 15-item transition self-rating had a sensitivity of 0.71 and a specificity of 0.68 for separation within 12 months of hire among 412 residents.
claims.passage: At a score of 30 or below, sensitivity was 0.71 (95 percent CI 0.60 to 0.81) and specificity 0.68 (0.63 to 0.73)
claims.interpretation: Planning values for local validation; the estimate comes from the data that chose the threshold and may be optimistic.

claims.text: Human resources separation dates were present and correct for 99 percent of nurses who left, so dates rather than reason codes can serve as the reference standard.
claims.passage: Separation dates were present and correct for 99 percent of nurses who left.
claims.interpretation: Define the target condition as leaving the hospital by date; do not rely on exit reason codes.

claims.text: The positive predictive value of a fixed transition threshold ranged from 0.21 to 0.44 as first-year separation varied from 12 to 27 percent between hospitals.
claims.passage: the positive predictive value ranged from 0.21 at 12 percent separation to 0.44 at 27 percent
claims.interpretation: Report predictive values at the local separation rate; a borrowed estimate would mislead the booster plan.

claims.text: Stated intention to leave identified fewer than half of early-career nurses who later separated.
claims.interpretation: Intention alone is a weak trigger; it is a comparison, not a replacement for the index test.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. One two-hospital study reports that a month-3 transition self-rating at 30 or below had sensitivity 0.71 and specificity 0.68 for separation within 12 months, with a positive predictive value of 0.35; a multi-hospital analysis shows predictive values shift with the local separation rate. The scale itself is reliable, human resources dates are an accurate reference standard when internal transfers are handled explicitly, and stated intention to leave misses about half of leavers. A booster tied to a low score was followed by better retention only in an uncontrolled comparison. The evidence supports measuring the accuracy of the cut-off locally before acting on it.
gradeRationale: One accuracy study with the threshold chosen in its own data, supported by measurement and reference-standard studies; imprecise and indirect for this hospital's separation rate. Certainty that the cut-off performs as reported here is low.
summary: Seven retrieved records appraised; four source-derived claims recorded with passages; overall certainty low.
